preamble: Palatalized [dʲ] (often from a d + yod sequence) frequently ends up as the voiced postalveolar fricative [ʒ], normally through an affricate stage [dʒ] that is later deaffricated. East Slavic turned Proto-Slavic *ď into ž (*meďa > Russian межа), and the Romance languages that deaffricated [dʒ] show the same endpoint from Latin -dj- / di-: Portuguese hoje < hodie, French jour < diurnum, Romanian jos < deorsum.

examples.note: Proto-Slavic *ď (< *dj) gives ž in East Slavic; also in the verbal alternation ходить ~ хожу [xɐˈʐu] 'walk'. Russian ж is phonetically retroflex [ʐ].
Latin -dj- gave [dʒ] in Old Galician-Portuguese, later deaffricated to [ʒ].
Initial di- > Old French [dʒ], simplified to [ʒ] in Middle French.
Developed via *di̯ósu > *djosu; the affricate [dʒ] became [ʒ] before a back vowel.
